Thanks for finding this.
I've been looking for it since the video of the speech was released. Much more accessible now in written form.

A few comments:

  • Hoppe suffers from the common libertarian malady of sectarianism by outright dismissing Minarchism and Classical Liberalism and only declaring his prticular flavour of Anarcho-Capitalism as "true" libertarianism. A transition to a libertarian society will take a long and hard road, and it will be hard enough with an united libertarian front. Fracturing before momentum can even be achieved will only aid authoritarians by divide and conquer. - Of course this isn't a new phenomenon about Hoppe, or about libertarians/AnCaps in general, but it is once again very apparent here.
  • I'm not really sold on his idea of small neighbourhoods undertaking collective action to initiate force against those who don't fit in. It would essentially trade the tyranny by a central democratically elected government for the tyranny by an land-owning aristocracy of a glorified HOA, which isn't much of an improvement from a libertarian POV. A community with a strong moral fiber can easily minimize the numbe of "bad neighbours" and make it clear to the few who enter that they are unwelcome without needing to fall back on force.
  • His idea of a libertarian populism is a very interesting one. I wonder if André Lichtschlag has been an influence on Hoppe here, as he has entertained some very similar ideas in his German libertarian magazine "Eigentümlich Frei" reflecting on the rise of Trump. - Of course this conflicts with his notion of striving only for "pure" libertarianism. A populist libertarian movement would need to be diffuse and diverse about its level of extremeness and need to be able to cater to moderate supporters as well, just as the Trump campaign managed to.
  • Banning weapon sales abroad and libertarian free trade don't mix at all. Either you have free industry and trade, including military weapons, or you have a central authority that intervenes into free trade, especially if you subscribe to such a radical flavour of libertarianism as Hoppe does.

Other than that, I have few reservations and criticisms. Hoppe is a good, nuanced thinker who can express his thoughts well, and his ability to blend high-minded libertarian principles with the realpolitik of acknowledging and adressing racial/cultural realities makes him unique in both the libertarian and the right-wing sphere.

Hoppe is a paleolibertarian, which could be described as reactionary libertarian or culturally conservative libertarian and putting him closer to NRx than to Libertarian Party libertarians. I quite like his writings.
